messages.author: 8dbb28b015bb7762
messages.subject: GRMFLib: Maximum number of evaluations
parts:
Hi Havard,

I'm getting 82 of this warnings sistematically with my dataset:

GMRFLib_ai_marginal_for_one_hyperparamter: warning:
Maximum number of function evaluations is reached
i=28, point=1.192, thread=0

where i goes from 0 to 40, the point varies and thread is always 0, and
all the warnings repeat once.

Do you know what is most likely causing this?
too close observations, maybe?

When I plot results I can see that there are empty spots where
prediction did not take place.

I am using the spde model, among other fixed and random effects:

formula = Y ~ 1 + P + C + f(spatial, model=spde) + f(A, model="iid") +
f(U, model="iid")

and running INLA with the following (mostly default) options

r = (inla(formula, family="binomial",
data = data,
lincomb = all.lc,
control.compute = list(return.marginals=FALSE),
control.inla=list(tolerance=1e-5),
verbose=FALSE
))

Do you have a suggestion about what settings I can try to fine-tune?

Thanks
Facundo.-

messages.author: 734f74f62919df1d
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] GRMFLib: Maximum number of evaluations
parts: On Jun 27, 2011, at 5:17 PM, Facundo Muñoz wrote:

>
> Hi Havard,
>
> I'm getting 82 of this warnings sistematically with my dataset:
>
> GMRFLib_ai_marginal_for_one_hyperparamter: warning:
> Maximum number of function evaluations is reached
> i=28, point=1.192, thread=0
>
> where i goes from 0 to 40, the point varies and thread is always 0, and
> all the warnings repeat once.
>
> Do you know what is most likely causing this?
> too close observations, maybe?
>

Hi

this is a warning only that the numerical integration to find the marginals for the hyperparameters, could not meet the tolerance requirements within the maximum number of function evaluations allowed.

see ?control.inla and these options

numint.maxfeval Maximum number of function evaluations in the the numerical integration for the hyperparameters. (Default 10000.)
numint.relerr Relative error requirement in the the numerical integration for the hyperparameters. (Default 1e-5)
numint.abserr Absolute error requirement in the the numerical integration for the hyperparameters. (Default 1e-6)

try to increase 'numint.maxfeval', like

inla(..., control.inla=list(numint.maxfeval = 10^6))

> When I plot results I can see that there are empty spots where
> prediction did not take place.
>
> Do you have a suggestion about what settings I can try to fine-tune?

in order to get the predictions, then you must turn that on, like

inla(..., control.predictor = list(compute=TRUE))

does this solve your problem ?

Best,
H
